subject: Export integrity & retention capabilities — RFI follow-up
messages:
From: Ethan Walker <ethan.walker@catalyst-payments.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@catalyst-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP question — exportability / tamper evidence / retention windows

Hi Tessa / Ben,

As part of Catalyst's RFP we need more detail on Redwood's capabilities around audit log exportability and retention provenance. Can you confirm the following items for our legal and forensics teams?

1) Retention window options per class (audit events, telemetry, admin actions) and whether retention is configurable per-customer/route.
2) Export formats supported for bulk exports (compressed ndjson, parquet, CSV) and whether metadata/headers are preserved.
3) Tamper-evidence: do exported bundles include signed manifests or other cryptographic proof we can use to verify integrity?
4) Chain-of-custody and delivery options (S3 presigned, SFTP, physical media) and typical delivery SLAs for large exports (100M+ events).
5) Support for customer-provided KMS keys for signing or at-rest encryption, plus attestations.

We'd appreciate examples of a manifest and verification steps if possible — our counsel needs to confirm admissibility in a regulated discovery process.

Thanks,
Ethan

Subject: Re: RFP question — exportability / tamper evidence / retention windows

Ethan — thanks for the clear list. I pulled Kim (security) and Ben (audit preservation) in, and we prepared a concise capability summary below and attached a small sample bundle for your legal team to exercise. Full technical runbook (confluence link) is available on request.

Short answers up front:
- Retention: configurable per-customer and per-log-class. Standard tiers: 30 days (hot), 90 days (nearline), 365 days (cold), and indefinite/legal-hold. Custom windows available by contract.
- Export formats: ndjson (preferred, preserves event-by-event metadata), gzipped ndjson, parquet (columnar), and CSV (less metadata). Each export bundle includes a machine-readable manifest.
- Tamper evidence: all bulk exports include a manifest listing file-level SHA-256 hashes plus a signed bundle digest. Manifests are signed using an HSM-backed key; we also provide an optional Merkle-tree proof for per-record verification.
- Delivery & SLA: delivery options include S3 (presigned), SFTP, or direct transfer to your cloud account. Small extracts (<100k events) typically within 24 hours; large full-harvests (100M+ events) standard SLA 5 business days (can be expedited).
- KMS & attestations: Redwood supports signing with Redwood-managed HSM keys or customer-provided asymmetric KMS keys (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS with asymmetric key material). We can provide attestation reports for Redwood HSMs (CA-signed certs) on request.

Implementation summary (more detail in attached sample):
- Packaging: export bundles are a tar.gz with: one or more data files (ndjson.gz), export_manifest.txt (manifest schema v1), and a signed_bundle.sig (PKCS7/ECDSA) that covers manifest digest.
- Manifest schema: manifest lists per-file SHA-256, record count, dataset timestamps (RFC3339), export parameters (time window, routes included), and a bundle UUID.
- Verification flow: (1) download bundle; (2) verify signed_bundle.sig against our public verification key (or a customer-provided verification key); (3) compare SHA-256 of each data file to manifest entries; (4) optional: run Merkle proof verification for sampled records.
- Chain-of-custody: manifest includes a time-stamped notarization field (UTC RFC3339) and an ordered event hash root; request logs include audit UUIDs to map back to live system.
- Redaction and selective export: we support redaction templates at export time (PII/tokenization) and can provide both redacted and raw (for legal) copies under an approved NDA.

Attaching a small sample bundle and a human-readable matrix (retention tiers) for your review. Ben and Kim will follow up with the tech appendix and a notarized sample if you need a court-ready package.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Compliance
Redwood Inference

Tessa — thanks, that is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from counsel and our security team: 

1) For the signed_bundle.sig: can you share the verification public key and an example command-line verification step (we need a reproducible procedure)?
2) Are the per-file SHA-256 hashes computed on the compressed file (ndjson.gz) or the uncompressed ndjson payload? Which do you recommend we verify?
3) For Merkle-tree proofs: is the tree built per-file or per-bundle, and do you provide tree leaves mapping to event offsets (so we can reproduce the same leaf hash from an exported record)?
4) KMS: if we provide an AWS KMS asymmetric key, can Redwood call KMS to perform signing (so the private material never leaves our account)?

If you can share a sample manifest and a short verification script (bash/python), that will speed legal review. Also, we'll want a quote for the expedited 48-hour harvest SLA as an add-on.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Ethan

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFP question — exportability / tamper evidence / retention windows

Ethan — answers inline and I attached the small verification helper and the public key: redwood_pub_verify.pem.

1) Verification: attached public key + simple verification steps in README_verify.txt. Example (bash):
   - sha256sum redwood_export_sample_v1.ndjson.gz > local.sha256
   - openssl dgst -sha256 -verify redwood_pub_verify.pem -signature signed_bundle.sig export_manifest.txt
   - compare the values in export_manifest.txt to local.sha256
   We included a short Python script (verify_export.py) that performs these steps and validates manifest schema v1.

2) Hashing: we compute SHA-256 over the compressed payload (ndjson.gz) to ensure byte-perfect delivery; manifest indicates whether hash is computed on compressed or uncompressed. For your verification, compute on the exact bytes of the file you received (we recommend verifying compressed file).

3) Merkle trees: by default we build per-file Merkle trees; leaves map to event-level hashes in order and include an index in the manifest so you can reproduce leaf hashes from event payloads. The manifest includes the tree root and a sample proof vector.

4) Customer KMS signing: yes — Redwood supports remote signing via customer-managed KMS asymmetric keys. Supported flows: (a) customer grants Redwood a limited signing role and Redwood calls AWS KMS Sign with the customer key (private never leaves KMS); (b) customer arranges for a signed manifest to be POSTed to Redwood during export initiation (bring-your-own-signature). We document the IAM role & approval flow in the appendix.

Deliverables attached: redwood_export_sample_v1.ndjson (sample payload), export_manifest_v1.txt (manifest with hash examples and merkle proof stub), redwood_pub_verify.pem (verification key), README_verify.txt, verify_export.py.

If you want a court-ready notarization we can produce a notarized manifest (time-stamped, HSM attestation) and chain-of-custody record — Ben can scope pricing. For the expedited SLA I'll ask Ops for a formal quote and will loop you in.

I can set up a 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow to run the verification live with your security team. What time works?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Compliance
Redwood Inference
